question: Is minibox a security boundary? Can you safely run untrusted code inside it?
answer_hinglish:
Seedha jawab: nahi. README ka pehla section hi 'Read this first: it is NOT a security boundary' hai, aur interview mein yeh baat sabse pehle bolni chahiye. minibox sab kuch real root ke roop mein chalata hai aur woh hardening karta hi nahi jo docker/runc karte hain.

Chaar cheezein missing hain: (1) user namespace nahi hai, toh container ka uid 0 host ka uid 0 hi hai -- test_user_namespace_is_shared_with_the_host yeh check karta hai. (2) Capabilities drop nahi hoti: CAP_SYS_ADMIN (mount kar sakta hai), CAP_SYS_MODULE (kernel module load), CAP_MKNOD (host disk ka device node bana sakta hai), CAP_SYS_PTRACE sab container ke paas hain. (3) Koi seccomp filter ya AppArmor/SELinux profile nahi, har syscall allowed hai. (4) cgroup namespace nahi, aur /sys mount nahi hai lekin container khud mount kar sakta hai.

Isliye koi bhi process bina exploit ke bahar nikal sakta hai, jaise mknod se host disk ka node banao aur mount kar lo. minibox ki isolation 'namespaces + pivot_root + cgroups' wala hissa hai: yeh samajhne ke liye kaafi hai ki docker kya karta hai, aur honest programs ek doosre ko na dekhein. Hostile program ke against protection nahi. README ki line: sirf woh code chalao jo aap host par root se waise bhi chala dete.
why_needed: Interviewer sabse pehle yahi pakadta hai: agar aap container ko 'secure sandbox' bol do toh credibility chali jaati hai. Limitation ko khud saaf bolna maturity dikhata hai.
real_world_analogy: Hotel room ka darwaza band hai (namespaces), lekin har guest ke paas master key hai (root + saari capabilities). Privacy milti hai, security nahi.
how_it_works: Container = normal process + naye namespaces + alag root filesystem + cgroup limits. Security ke layers alag hain: user namespace (uid mapping), capability bounding set, seccomp (syscall filter), LSM profile (AppArmor/SELinux), masked/readonly paths, no_new_privs. minibox inmein se koi layer nahi lagata.
in_this_project: cli.py ka main() root na ho toh mana kar deta hai: 'run needs root (no user namespace support), use sudo'. README ka security section aur NOT implemented list dono yeh likhte hain, aur ek integration test limitation ko sach rakhta hai.
code_example:
# real, tests/integration/test_isolation.py
def test_user_namespace_is_shared_with_the_host(box):
    # stated limitation, checked so the README stays true: root in the box IS root on the host
    r = box.run("readlink /proc/self/ns/user; id -u")
    assert r.stdout.split() == [os.readlink("/proc/self/ns/user"), "0"]
advantages: Limitation documented aur test se pinned hai
Learning ke liye har syscall visible, koi hidden hardening nahi
disadvantages: Untrusted code ke liye bilkul unsafe
Root ke bina chalta hi nahi (rootless nahi)
common_mistakes: Namespaces ko hi security maan lena
pivot_root ko 'escape-proof' bolna jabki baaki raste khule hain
Docker jaisa dikhne ko docker jaisa secure samajhna
follow_up_questions: Agar ise multi-tenant banana ho toh pehla kaunsa layer jodoge aur kyun?
Container ke andar root aur host ke root mein user namespace ke saath kya farak aata hai?
Docker ka default setup bhi poori tarah hostile code ke liye kaafi kyun nahi maana jaata?

question: Walk through how a process inside minibox could reach the host's disk without any exploit. Which missing protections make it possible?
answer_hinglish:
README ek concrete raasta deta hai: 'mknod the host disk, mount it'. Steps samjho. Container ke andar process uid 0 hai aur host ke same user namespace mein hai. Uske paas CAP_MKNOD hai, toh woh /dev mein (jo minibox ka tmpfs hai) host ki disk ke major/minor number ke saath ek block device node bana sakta hai. Device node sirf ek pointer hai; kernel us number se seedha host ki asli disk par le jaata hai. Phir CAP_SYS_ADMIN hai, toh woh us node ko container ke andar kisi directory par mount kar sakta hai aur host ka filesystem padh/likh sakta hai.

minibox ne kya kiya hai: mounts.py ki DEVICES list mein sirf null, zero, full, random, urandom, tty hain (wahi chhota set jo runc banata hai), aur test_host_block_devices_are_absent check karta hai ki /dev/sda, /dev/vda, /dev/nvme0n1, /dev/mem container mein nahi dikhte. Lekin yeh sirf 'by default absent' hai, 'prevented' nahi. Fark interview mein bolna zaroori hai.

Rokne ke liye kya chahiye hota (minibox mein NAHI kiya): CAP_MKNOD aur CAP_SYS_ADMIN drop karna, device cgroup / BPF device filter jo naye block devices ko deny kare, user namespace (jisme naya mknod host devices ke liye kaam nahi karta), aur seccomp jo mount jaise syscalls ko rok de.
why_needed: Yeh question check karta hai ki aap 'device not visible' aur 'device not accessible' ka farak samajhte ho ya nahi.
real_world_analogy: Ghar se TV hata diya, lekin bijli ka plug aur cable wall mein hai: koi bhi naya TV laakar laga sakta hai.
how_it_works: Device node = inode jisme type (char/block) + major/minor hai. open() par kernel major/minor se driver dhoondhta hai. Isse rokne waale kernel checks: capability (CAP_MKNOD), device cgroup permissions, aur LSM. Mount ke liye CAP_SYS_ADMIN chahiye.
in_this_project: build_plan /dev par tmpfs mount karta hai aur sirf DEVICES list ke nodes banata hai; apply_step Mknod ke liye os.mknod chalata hai. Koi capability drop ya device filter code mein nahi hai.
code_example:
# real, minibox/mounts.py
# (name, major, minor): the same small set runc creates
DEVICES = [("null", 1, 3), ("zero", 1, 5), ("full", 1, 7), ("random", 1, 8), ("urandom", 1, 9), ("tty", 5, 0)]
advantages: Default /dev chhota hai, host disks dikhte nahi
Test absence ko pin karta hai
disadvantages: Absence != prevention; root + CAP_MKNOD sab bana sakta hai
Koi device cgroup filter nahi
common_mistakes: Sochna ki host /dev bind na karne se disk safe hai
CAP_SYS_ADMIN ko sirf 'admin flag' samajhna, jabki yeh mount deta hai
follow_up_questions: Device cgroup v2 mein files se nahi, BPF program se kaise hota hai?
User namespace ke andar mknod se host disk kyun nahi khulti?
CAP_SYS_ADMIN drop karne se minibox ka kaunsa apna setup step toot jaata agar order galat ho?

question: If you had to turn minibox into something closer to a real sandbox, what would docker/runc add on top of it, and in what order would you do it?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle saaf: yeh sab minibox mein NAHI hai; README ki NOT implemented list mein likha hai -- user namespaces (rootless), capability dropping, seccomp, AppArmor/SELinux, read-only rootfs, no_new_privs, /proc/kcore jaisi paths ki masking. Toh yeh 'kya chahiye hoga' ka answer hai, 'kya kiya' ka nahi.

Mera order: (1) User namespace -- container ka uid 0 host par ek unprivileged uid (jaise 100000) ho. Isse sabse bada risk (root = host root, jo test_user_namespace_is_shared_with_the_host aaj prove karta hai) khatam hota hai, aur capabilities sirf namespace ke andar valid rehti hain. (2) Capability bounding set ko docker jaise chhote default set tak drop karna: CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_MKNOD hatao. Yeh setup_container ke BAAD aur exec se pehle karna padega, kyunki minibox ka apna setup (mount, pivot_root, sethostname) inhi capabilities par chalta hai. (3) no_new_privs (prctl) taaki setuid binaries privilege na badha sakein. (4) Seccomp filter -- docker ka default profile kai syscalls block karta hai (jaise kexec, module load, kai mount variants). (5) Masked paths: /proc/kcore, /proc/sys jaise files ko /dev/null bind ya read-only karna. (6) AppArmor/SELinux profile, read-only rootfs option, aur cgroup namespace.

Order kyun: user namespace sabse zyada risk kam karta hai; seccomp aur LSM defense in depth hain.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki aapko pata hai docker 'namespaces + cgroups' ke upar kitni layers lagata hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank vault: namespaces sirf alag kamre hain. User ns = guard ki uniform badal di (bahar koi power nahi), caps drop = chaabiyan le li, seccomp = kuch darwaze hi seal kar diye, LSM = CCTV + rulebook.
how_it_works: runc config.json mein namespaces, uid/gid mappings, capabilities (bounding/effective/permitted), seccomp profile, maskedPaths, readonlyPaths, noNewPrivileges, apparmorProfile hote hain. runc in sab ko exec se theek pehle apply karta hai, jab uska apna setup ho chuka ho.
in_this_project: init_main mein setup_container ke baad aur os.execvpe se pehle ka hissa hi woh jagah hai jahan yeh steps aate. Aaj wahan sirf signal reset, chdir aur exec hai. PLAN.md 'Not in scope' mein bhi yeh list hai.
code_example:
# real, minibox/container.py setup_container (no hardening step exists after this)
def setup_container(cfg: Config, plan: mounts.Plan) -> None:
    os.unshare(os.CLONE_NEWNS | os.CLONE_NEWUTS | os.CLONE_NEWIPC | os.CLONE_NEWNET)
    socket.sethostname(cfg.hostname)
    bring_up_loopback()
    mounts.apply_plan(plan)
    mounts.enter_root(plan.new_root, use_pivot_root=cfg.use_pivot_root)
advantages: Saaf insertion point hai (setup ke baad, exec se pehle)
Har layer alag se test ho sakti hai
disadvantages: Python stdlib mein seccomp/capset ka wrapper nahi, aur ctypes chahiye
User ns ke saath overlay aur cgroup permissions complex ho jaate hain
common_mistakes: Caps ko setup se PEHLE drop kar dena, phir mount fail
Seccomp ko akela kaafi maan lena
Yeh claim karna ki minibox mein yeh already hai
follow_up_questions: User namespace ke saath overlayfs mount karne mein kya dikkat aati hai?
no_new_privs na ho toh setuid binary ka risk kya hai?
Docker ka default seccomp profile tod kar koi app chalani pade toh kya karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Har layer security badhati hai lekin compatibility todti hai: seccomp kuch apps ke syscalls rok deta hai, user ns file ownership (overlay upper, image uid 0) ko complex banata hai. minibox ne learning ke liye sab visible rakha.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Galat order: agar CAP_SYS_ADMIN setup_container se pehle drop ho toh mount/pivot_root EPERM se fail aur exit 125. Seccomp profile mein ek zaroori syscall chhoot gaya toh app random jagah crash karegi.
advanced.alternatives: Full VM ya microVM (Firecracker), gVisor jaisa user-space kernel, ya rootless podman jo user ns default rakhta hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada containers par per-container seccomp/LSM profile manage karna padta hai; ek central default profile + per-workload override chahiye. uid range allocation bhi har container ke liye unique rakhni padegi.
advanced.production_improvements: Har hardening step ke saath ek 'negative' integration test (jaise mknod ab EPERM deta hai), jaise aaj test_user_namespace_is_shared_with_the_host limitation ko pin karta hai. Mutation checks bhi har layer ke liye.

question: Why does the test suite contain a test that proves a LIMITATION (root in the container is root on the host) instead of only testing features?
answer_hinglish:
test_user_namespace_is_shared_with_the_host container ke andar 'readlink /proc/self/ns/user; id -u' chalata hai aur assert karta hai ki user namespace ka inode host jaisa hi hai aur uid 0 hai. Comment mein likha hai: 'stated limitation, checked so the README stays true'.

Iska maqsad documentation ko code se baandhna hai. README bolta hai 'No user namespace. Root in the container is root on the host'. Agar kal koi CLONE_NEWUSER jod de, toh yeh test red hoga aur dev ko README update karna padega. Ulta bhi: agar koi galti se sochta hai ki isolation zyada hai, test dikhata hai ki nahi hai. Yeh 'honest' documentation ka tareeka hai -- claims ko assertion bana do.

Isi pattern ka doosra example: test_container_runs_in_its_own_cgroup mein comment hai 'no cgroup namespace (see README), so the full host path is visible' aur test expect karta hai '0::/minibox/<name>'. Yani missing cgroup namespace bhi test mein dikh raha hai. Aur test_every_namespace_differs_from_the_host sirf pid, uts, ipc, mnt, net ko check karta hai, user ko nahi -- jo exact claim hai.
why_needed: Docs aur code alag-alag drift karte hain. Limitation ko test karne se README ki security warning kabhi jhooti nahi banti.
real_world_analogy: Building par board 'Lift sirf 4 log' -- aur lift khud 5th person par alarm bajati hai. Board aur machine ek hi baat bolte hain.
how_it_works: Har namespace /proc/self/ns/<type> par ek symlink jaisa 'user:[inode]' dikhata hai. Do processes same namespace mein hain agar inode same hai. Test host ke readlink se container ka output compare karta hai.
in_this_project: container.py ka setup_container unshare mein CLONE_NEWUSER pass nahi karta; host side sirf CLONE_NEWPID. Test usi ko pin karta hai.
code_example:
# real, tests/integration/test_limits.py (trimmed)
def test_container_runs_in_its_own_cgroup(box):
    # no cgroup namespace (see README), so the full host path is visible. Repeated, because the bug
    # this guards against (the command forked before INIT joined the cgroup) is a race.
    for i in range(10):
        r = box.run("cat /proc/self/cgroup", "--name", f"cg-path-{i}")
        assert r.stdout.strip() == f"0::/minibox/cg-path-{i}", f"run {i}: {r.stdout!r}"
advantages: README claims aur behaviour sync rehte hain
Future change ko conscious decision banata hai
disadvantages: Kuch log ise 'bug ko test karna' samajh kar hata dete hain
Test fail hone par message clear hona chahiye ki docs bhi badlo
common_mistakes: Limitation ko sirf README mein likh kar chhod dena
Test ko negative assertion se 'sab theek hai' samajhna
follow_up_questions: Yeh test kab aur kaise badlega agar user namespace add ho?
Aur kaunsi README claim ko aap test bana sakte ho?

question: pivot_root defeats the chroot escape in the tests. Why is that still not enough to call minibox's filesystem isolation secure?
answer_hinglish:
Do tests hain: test_chroot_alone_can_be_escaped (control: chroot ke saath classic escape -- mkdir, chroot without chdir, 64 baar '..', chroot('.') -- host ki marker file tak pahunch jaata hai) aur test_pivot_root_cannot_be_escaped (wahi escape pivot_root ke baad fail). Mutation M1 (pivot_root ko chroot se badlo) pehle test ko red karta hai. Toh ek specific raasta band hai.

Lekin README khud likhta hai: 'pivot_root stops THIS path out; with all capabilities kept, a root process can still get out other ways'. Kaunse? (1) CAP_SYS_ADMIN se naye mounts: /sys ya proc ke sensitive hisse, ya mknod kiya hua host disk. (2) /proc fresh hai lekin masked paths nahi -- /proc/sys ya /proc/kcore jaisi files par koi masking nahi. (3) cgroup namespace nahi, toh container /sys/fs/cgroup mount karke host ki cgroup hierarchy dekh sakta hai. (4) CAP_SYS_PTRACE aur CAP_SYS_MODULE bhi hain; module load = kernel ke andar code.

Toh pivot_root filesystem 'view' ko alag karta hai, privilege ko nahi. Security tab aati hai jab process ke paas naye mounts aur device access ki power hi na ho. Interview line: pivot_root ek zaroori condition hai, sufficient nahi.
why_needed: Ek attack test pass karna aur 'secure' hona alag cheezein hain; interviewer threat model ki depth dekhta hai.
real_world_analogy: Jail ki ek deewar majboot kar di, lekin qaidi ke paas abhi bhi drill machine (CAP_SYS_ADMIN) hai.
how_it_works: pivot_root namespace ka root mount swap karta hai; old root /.oldroot par jaata hai aur umount2(MNT_DETACH) se hat jaata hai, toh climb karne ko host tree bachta hi nahi. Par mount(2) syscall abhi bhi allowed hai.
in_this_project: mounts.enter_root mein pivot_root + chdir + umount2 + rmdir; use_pivot_root=False sirf test ke liye. Test _escape_attempt forked child mein setup_container chala kar escape try karta hai.
code_example:
# real, minibox/mounts.py enter_root (trimmed)
if use_pivot_root:
    put_old = os.path.join(new_root, OLD_ROOT)
    libc.pivot_root(new_root, put_old)
    os.chdir("/")
    libc.umount2("/" + OLD_ROOT, libc.MNT_DETACH)
    os.rmdir("/" + OLD_ROOT)
else:
    os.chdir(new_root)
    os.chroot(".")
    os.chdir("/")
advantages: Escape test ke saath control experiment bhi hai
Old root detach hota hai (M2 isko pakadta hai)
disadvantages: Mount/mknod privilege abhi bhi hai
No masked paths, no cgroup ns
common_mistakes: Ek passing escape test ko 'escape-proof' bolna
Control test ke bina pivot_root test likhna (woh kuch prove nahi karta)
follow_up_questions: Control test fail ho jaaye toh pivot_root wala test kya prove karta hai?
/sys ko read-only mount karna kaafi hoga ya mount syscall hi rokna padega?
Masked paths runc mein kaise implement hote hain?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: minibox ne filesystem view ko sahi tareeke se alag kiya (pivot_root + detach) aur privilege isolation ko scope se bahar rakha. Fayda: code chhota aur har step test hua. Nuksan: koi bhi privileged syscall poora isolation tod sakta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Container mount -t sysfs ya mknod + mount karke host data padh sakta hai; README is raaste ko naam se likhta hai. M2 (old root not detached) mein /.oldroot mount list mein dikh jaata, jo mount-list test pakadta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Caps drop + seccomp mount ko block kare; user ns mein mounts sirf namespace-owned filesystems tak limited; read-only rootfs aur masked paths (runc style).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut saare tenants par ek escape sabko affect karta hai, toh har layer (user ns, seccomp, LSM) default-on chahiye, per-container opt-out nahi.
advanced.production_improvements: Escape attempts ki ek test family: mknod disk, mount sysfs, write /proc/sys -- har ek ke liye 'ab EPERM' assert, aur mutation check jo har hardening line hata kar red dikhaye.

question: How are minibox's tests split, and why can most of them run on a Windows PC even though containers need Linux?
answer_hinglish:
Do level hain. 140 unit tests jo kahin bhi chalte hain (Windows bhi; 5 Windows par skip hote hain -- symlinks aur POSIX modes ke liye), aur 52 integration tests jo Linux + root + ek image rootfs maangte hain.

Trick design mein hai: jo cheez pure logic hai use data bana do. mounts.build_plan mount steps ko Mount / Mkdir / Mknod / Symlink dataclasses ki list ke roop mein return karta hai -- order aur flags test_mounts.py mein Windows par check hote hain (test_first_step_makes_everything_private, test_root_before_proc_before_dev_and_oldroot_last). Limits.writes() exact (file, value) pairs deta hai, jaise memory.max = 67108864 aur memory.swap.max = 0. Cgroup class ko ek fake root directory di ja sakti hai, toh test_create_writes_limits_into_a_leaf_on_a_fake_root normal folder par chal jaata hai. Registry ke liye fake fetch function, image ke liye fixture layer tars. libc.py libc ko lazily load karta hai taaki Windows par import fail na ho.

Integration tests asli kaam check karte hain: namespaces, pivot_root escape, OOM kill 137, pids.peak 32, overlay whiteouts. Woh portfolio-a2 server par chale. Final clean run: 192/192 (140 + 52).
why_needed: Dev PC Windows hai; agar har test ke liye server chahiye ho toh feedback loop bahut slow ho jaata.
real_world_analogy: Car ka engine design table par (unit) check karo, aur test track par sirf asli drive (integration).
how_it_works: Functional core / imperative shell: plan banana pure function, plan apply karna side effect. Pure hissa har OS par fast test, side-effect hissa sirf target environment mein.
in_this_project: pyproject.toml mein markers 'integration' aur 'network' declared hain; conftest integration tests ko automatically mark aur zaroorat ho toh skip karta hai. README ka 'Run it' section dono commands deta hai.
advantages: Fast feedback Windows par
Order aur flags jaise subtle rules unit level par pinned
disadvantages: Unit test sirf intent check karta hai, kernel ka behaviour nahi
Integration ke liye server chahiye
common_mistakes: Sab kuch mock karke maan lena ki container kaam karta hai
Plan ko data na bana kar seedhe syscalls likhna, phir test na kar paana
follow_up_questions: Ek bug jo sirf integration test pakad sakta hai, uska example do.
libc ko lazily load karna Windows unit tests ke liye kyun zaroori tha?

question: The integration conftest SKIPS tests with a reason instead of failing them when it is not on Linux/root/with a rootfs. Why that choice, and what is the risk?
answer_hinglish:
conftest.py ka pytest_collection_modifyitems har test jo 'integration' folder mein hai use pytest.mark.integration deta hai, aur agar environment theek nahi toh pytest.mark.skip ek specific reason ke saath: 'integration tests need Linux', 'integration tests need root (sudo)', ya 'set MINIBOX_TEST_ROOTFS to an alpine/busybox rootfs (python -m minibox pull alpine:3.20 --dest D)'. Rootfs ki check bhi concrete hai: ROOTFS/bin/busybox file honi chahiye.

Kyun skip: Windows dev PC par 'python -m pytest' ek hi command se chalna chahiye, 140 unit pass aur 52 skip, red nahi. Agar fail karte toh har local run red hota aur log asli failures ko ignore karna seekh jaate. Reason message ek tarah ka instruction hai -- kya karna hai woh batata hai, jaise rootfs kaise pull karo.

Risk: skip silent green ban sakta hai. Agar server par MINIBOX_TEST_ROOTFS set karna bhool gaye, toh suite 'pass' dikhega jabki 52 tests chale hi nahi. Is project mein yeh count se cover hua: server run mein '192 passed (140 unit + 52 integration)' explicitly dekha gaya. CI mein isko 'skips allowed = 0 on the Linux job' jaisi rule se pakka karna chahiye -- yeh minibox mein nahi hai.
why_needed: Ek suite do environments mein chalni hai; galat environment mein false red bhi bura hai aur false green bhi.
real_world_analogy: Exam mein 'yeh question aapke syllabus mein nahi' likh kar chhod dena theek hai, lekin result card par count dikhna chahiye ki kitne chhode.
how_it_works: pytest collection ke baad hook items ki list deta hai; marker add karna run se pehle hota hai. skip marker test ko execute hi nahi karta, sirf report mein 's' aur reason dikhata hai (-rs se).
in_this_project: pyproject.toml mein markers declared hain taaki unknown-marker warning na aaye; test_pull_alpine_from_docker_hub par alag 'network' marker hai.
advantages: Ek command har jagah
Skip reason actionable hai
disadvantages: Silent green ka risk agar env var bhool gaye
Skip count ko koi gate nahi karta
common_mistakes: Environment check ko har test ke andar duplicate karna
Skip ko fail jaisa 'theek hai' maan kar count na dekhna
follow_up_questions: Linux CI job mein skipped integration tests ko fail kaise karoge?
Rootfs check ke liye bin/busybox hi kyun dekha?

question: What does the no_leftovers fixture do, and why does it KILL leftover containers before failing the test instead of just failing?
answer_hinglish:
no_leftovers ek autouse fixture hai, toh har integration test ke baad chalta hai. Woh do cheezein check karta hai: /sys/fs/cgroup/minibox ke neeche koi cgroup bacha hai kya, aur /proc/self/mounts mein koi '/state/' ya 'minibox' wali mount bachi hai kya.

Interesting hissa order hai. Agar cgroups bache, toh pehle har ek ke cgroup.kill mein '1' likhta hai (kernel us cgroup ke saare processes SIGKILL karta hai), 10 second tak wait karta hai ki host-side minibox process INIT ki maut dekh kar khud cgroup hataye, jo phir bhi bacha use khud rmdir karta hai, phir parent rmdir try karta hai, aur TAB assert fail karta hai 'cgroups left behind (killed now)'.

Yeh server incident se aaya (SERVER_RUN.md incident 3, 18:10): mutation M6 mein INIT SIGTERM forward nahi karta tha, test ka container kabhi ruka nahi, aur do containers chalte reh gaye. Agle mutation runs ne unke cgroups dekhe aur galat reason se fail hue. Unhe haath se cgroup.kill likh kar roka gaya. Fix: fixture ab kill + remove pehle karta hai, taaki ek toota test baaki suite ko contaminate na kare. M6 aur M8-M11 phir clean server par re-run hue; README table mein re-run numbers hain, aur '2 + 2 errors' jaise entries isi fixture ke errors hain.
why_needed: Shared server par ek failed test ke chhode hue processes agle saare tests ka result kharab kar dete hain.
real_world_analogy: Kitchen mein har cook ke baad inspector chulha band karta hai PEHLE, phir report likhta hai 'gas khula chhoda tha'. Sirf report likhne se agla cook aag mein kaam karega.
how_it_works: cgroup.kill (kernel 5.14+) cgroup ke saare processes ko ek saath SIGKILL karta hai, race-free, pids ki list padhe bina. Empty cgroup dir rmdir se hat jaati hai.
in_this_project: Fixture container.py ke cleanup jaisa hi kaam karta hai lekin test ke level par, aur fail karke batata bhi hai. Mounts check isliye ki M4 jaisi galti host namespace mein mounts leak kar deti hai.
code_example:
# real, tests/integration/conftest.py no_leftovers (trimmed)
# Kill what a failed test left running BEFORE failing it, so one broken test (or a deliberate
# mutation) cannot leave containers running on the server and break every later test.
for d in left:
    with open(f"{base}/{d}/cgroup.kill", "w") as f:
        f.write("1")
deadline = time.monotonic() + 10
while any(os.path.isdir(f"{base}/{d}") for d in left) and time.monotonic() < deadline:
    time.sleep(0.05)
...
assert not left, f"cgroups left behind (killed now): {left}"
advantages: Failures isolated rehte hain
Server saaf rehta hai, haath se cleanup nahi
disadvantages: Fixture khud ek cleanup implementation hai jisme bug ho sakta hai
10 s deadline slow failure de sakti hai
common_mistakes: Leak detect karke sirf assert karna, kill nahi
Cleanup ko sirf success path par rakhna
follow_up_questions: Fixture ka rmdir kab zaroori hota hai jab host-side minibox process khud nahi hata paata?
Mounts leak check '/state/' string par kyun depend karta hai, iski limitation kya hai?

question: What is mutation testing, and how was it done for minibox?
answer_hinglish:
Mutation testing ka idea simple hai: code mein jaan bujh kar ek bug daalo aur dekho ki koi test red hota hai ya nahi. Agar koi test red nahi hua, toh woh rule actually test nahi ho raha -- coverage number kuch bhi bole.

minibox mein 29 mutation checks hue (README 'Mutation checks', 2026-11-21, portfolio-a2 par). Method: har rule ko SERVER WALI COPY mein toda gaya, repo mein kabhi nahi; relevant tests root se chalaye; phir clean tree dobara ship kiya gaya. Check pass tab hai jab kam se kam ek test red ho. Runner PC ke scratch folder mein tha, repo mein nahi.

Examples: M1 pivot_root ko chroot se badla -> 1 test red (escape test). M3 /proc remount hataya -> 12 red. M15 memory.swap.max nahi likha -> 2 red (hog swap karke bach jaata, server par 4 GB swap hai). M20 layer digest check hataya -> 2 red. Result: 28 of 29 caught; M18 (cleanup mein cgroup.kill skip) nahi pakda gaya, aur README iski wajah honestly likhta hai. Mutation ke baad clean tree ne full suite pass kiya: 192/192.
why_needed: Tests pass hona yeh prove nahi karta ki tests kuch check karte hain; mutation yeh prove karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Smoke detector test karne ke liye button dabate ho ya thoda dhuan dikhate ho. Bajaa nahi toh detector bekaar hai.
how_it_works: Mutant = code ki ek chhoti badli hui copy. Killed = kisi test ne fail kiya. Survived = sab green. Mutation score = killed / total. Yahan hand-written targeted mutants hain (tool-generated random nahi).
in_this_project: Config mein use_pivot_root, reap_zombies, forward_signals jaise switches tests ke liye hain, lekin mutation checks inke alawa server copy ke source mein seedhe edit the.
advantages: Har important rule ke liye proof ki test usse pakadta hai
Repo kabhi mutate nahi hua
disadvantages: Hand-written mutants sirf woh pakadte hain jo aapne socha
Har mutation ke liye server run chahiye
common_mistakes: Coverage percentage ko test quality samajhna
Mutation ko repo mein karke galti se commit kar dena
follow_up_questions: M18 kyun nahi pakda gaya?
Tool-based mutation testing (mutmut jaisa) yahan kyun use nahi kiya hoga?
Kisi mutation ka 'errors' count kya matlab rakhta hai?

question: The mutation table says '28 of 29 caught'. What does that headline NOT tell you, and how should you read the individual rows (M18, M26, M28, the 'errors' column, the mutations that were never run)?
answer_hinglish:
Headline number akela misleading ho sakta hai; README ka 'What the table does NOT show, honestly' section isi liye hai. Row by row padhna padta hai.

(1) M18 (cleanup skips cgroup.kill) survived -- lekin yeh test gap nahi, equivalent mutant hai: PID 1 ke exit par kernel namespace ke saare processes maar deta hai, toh cleanup ke time cgroup already khaali hai. (2) M26 ('..' in tar names not refused) sirf name-check ke unit test se pakda gaya; apply time par tarfile ka apna 'tar' filter bhi '../x' refuse karta, toh yeh 'two lines of defense' hain -- ek hata do toh doosri bachaati hai, isliye integration level par mutant dikhta nahi. (3) M28 ka count sirf 1 hai lekin woh important hai: tarfile ka 'tar' filter as-is use karne se modes strip hote, aur 1777 /tmp 0755 ban jaata. (4) 'errors' column (M4: 2 + 2 errors, M6: 2 + 2, M7: 2 + 3) test failures nahi, no_leftovers fixture ke findings hain -- broken code ne containers ya mounts chhode. Yeh failed count se alag signal hai: mutant ne SIDE EFFECT bhi kiya. (5) Jo mutations chalaye hi nahi: UTS namespace flag (bina uske sethostname asli server ka naam badal deta), aur fork bomb test kisi bhi mutation ke saath nahi chala.

Aur ek practical check: M17 ka pehla version SyntaxError tha (9/9 red galat reason se), re-run 'pass' ke saath 2 red. Toh count ke saath reason bhi verify karo.
why_needed: Interview mein metric ko blindly quote karne ke bajaye uski limitations batana judgement dikhata hai.
real_world_analogy: Exam result '28/29 pass' -- lekin ek subject ka paper hi nahi hua, aur ek mein do teachers ne check kiya. Report card ke footnotes zaroori hain.
how_it_works: Mutation table ke columns: mutation, tests run (scope), failed. Equivalent mutant = behaviour observably same; redundant check = do independent guards, ek ka mutant doosre se mask hota hai; side-effect errors = fixture ne leak pakda.
in_this_project: README 'Mutation checks' table aur uske neeche ki list; image.py mein clean_member_path (name check) aur tarfile filter dono; conftest no_leftovers 'errors' generate karta hai.
advantages: Honest reading se real gaps dikhte hain
Errors column side effects ko alag dikhata hai
disadvantages: Hand-made mutants ki list khud biased ho sakti hai
Kuch dangerous mutations jaan bujh kar untested
common_mistakes: Mutation score ko coverage ki tarah ek number bana dena
Equivalent mutant ko 'test likhna bhool gaye' samajhna
Redundant defenses mein se ek ko hata kar kehna 'test hi nahi tha'
follow_up_questions: M26 ko integration level par pakadne ke liye kya karna padega?
Kya redundant defense rakhna accha hai agar woh mutation testing ko blind kar de?
UTS mutation ko safely kaise test karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Hand-written targeted mutants high signal dete hain lekin sirf woh rules cover karte hain jo socha gaya. Tool-based random mutants zyada broad hote lekin noisy, aur root + server ke saath slow.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar sirf headline dekho toh M18 jaisa redundant code future refactor mein hat sakta hai bina kisi ko pata chale; M26 mein agar tarfile ka behaviour badle (Python version) toh ek defense chali jaati hai.
advanced.alternatives: mutmut/cosmic-ray jaise tools unit level par; integration level par hand mutants jaisa yahan.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bade codebase par per-rule mutation catalog maintain karna padega, aur runs parallel + isolated (VM per mutant).
advanced.production_improvements: Table mein 'reason verified' column, equivalent/redundant mutants ka explicit tag, aur destructive tests ka documented exclusion list jo runner enforce kare.

question: Mutation M3 skipped remounting /proc and turned 12 isolation tests red. Why does one missing mount break so much, and why must /proc be mounted AFTER the new PID namespace exists?
answer_hinglish:
Plan ka step 3: proc ko new_root/proc par mount karo, nosuid + noexec + nodev ke saath. README: 'a fresh procfs shows only the new PID namespace; the image's empty /proc would show nothing (M3: 12 tests red)'.

Kyun itne tests: bahut saare integration tests apna evidence /proc se padhte hain. test_every_namespace_differs_from_the_host /proc/self/ns/<ns> padhta hai; test_command_is_pid_2_and_init_is_pid_1 /proc/1/cmdline; test_proc_is_fresh_and_shows_only_the_container 'ls /proc'; test_only_the_containers_own_mounts_are_visible /proc/mounts; test_only_loopback_network_and_it_is_up /proc/net/dev; IPC test /proc/sysvipc/shm; orphan reaping test /proc/[0-9]*/status. /dev ke symlinks (fd -> /proc/self/fd, stdin -> /proc/self/fd/0) bhi /proc par depend karte hain. Toh /proc gaya toh observability gayi -- 12 red.

Timing: procfs mount ke waqt mounting process ke PID namespace se bind hota hai. INIT naye PID namespace ka PID 1 hai (host ne unshare(CLONE_NEWPID) karke fork kiya), aur setup_container INIT ke andar chalta hai, toh yeh proc sirf container ke processes dikhata hai. Unit test test_proc_is_mounted_inside_new_root_with_safe_flags target aur flags pin karta hai, aur test_root_before_proc_before_dev_and_oldroot_last order (private, overlay, proc, tmpfs, devpts, tmpfs).
why_needed: /proc container ka 'dashboard' hai; ps, top, aur bahut tools isi par chalte hain. Galat proc = galat view, ya host ka view leak.
real_world_analogy: Naye office mein purane office ka notice board laga diya: ya toh khaali hai ya purane logon ke naam dikhata hai.
how_it_works: procfs har mount par apne PID namespace se bandha hota hai. Host ka /proc bind karne se host ke saare PIDs dikhte. Image ka /proc sirf ek khaali directory hai.
in_this_project: mounts.build_plan mein Mkdir(proc) + Mount('proc', ..., MS_NOSUID|MS_NOEXEC|MS_NODEV); mount_proc=False sirf test (test_proc_can_be_left_out) ke liye.
code_example:
# real, tests/unit/test_mounts.py
def test_proc_is_mounted_inside_new_root_with_safe_flags():
    plan = build_plan(ROOT, overlay())
    proc = [m for m in mounts_of(plan) if m.fstype == "proc"]
    assert len(proc) == 1
    assert proc[0].target == os.path.join(plan.new_root, "proc")
    assert proc[0].flags == libc.MS_NOSUID | libc.MS_NOEXEC | libc.MS_NODEV
advantages: Fresh proc = sahi PID view
Order aur flags unit level par pinned
disadvantages: /proc abhi bhi masked nahi (/proc/sys, /proc/kcore) -- security hardening nahi
common_mistakes: Host ka /proc bind mount kar dena
proc ko PID namespace banne se pehle mount karna
Sochna ki ps ke bina container theek hai toh /proc zaroori nahi
follow_up_questions: /proc ko read-only ya masked banane ke liye kya karna padega?
M3 jaise ek mutant ka 12 tests todna accha signal hai ya noisy?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Fresh proc mount sasta aur zaroori hai; lekin bina masking ke poora procfs container ko milta hai (README NOT-done: masking /proc/kcore and friends).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar proc PID namespace se pehle mount hota (jaise host process mein), toh host ke PIDs dikhte. Agar mount hi na ho toh ps/top/self-introspection tootte, aur /dev/fd symlinks dangling.
advanced.alternatives: runc config.json mein proc mount + maskedPaths + readonlyPaths; ya hidepid options.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut containers par har ek ka apna procfs instance cheap hai; lekin monitoring agents jo host /proc padhte hain unhe namespace-aware hona chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: maskedPaths (/proc/kcore, /proc/keys, etc.) ko /dev/null bind, /proc/sys read-only, aur integration test jo un paths par write fail assert kare.

question: The pivot_root escape test is paired with a test that EXPECTS the chroot escape to succeed. Why is that control test necessary, and what did mutation M1 show?
answer_hinglish:
_escape_attempt ek forked child mein asli setup_container chalata hai (use_pivot_root True ya False), check karta hai ki host-only marker file abhi nahi dikh rahi, phir classic escape try karta hai: mkdir('/escape-dir'), chroot('/escape-dir') bina chdir ke (cwd ab new root ke BAHAR hai), 64 baar chdir('..'), chroot('.'). Phir marker dikhti hai ya nahi, woh pipe se '1'/'0' wapas bhejta hai.

test_pivot_root_cannot_be_escaped expect karta hai False. Lekin sirf yeh test ho toh ek problem hai: agar escape code hi galat likha ho (jaise marker path galat, ya chroot kabhi chala hi nahi), toh bhi False aayega aur test green -- kuch prove nahi. Isliye test_chroot_alone_can_be_escaped control experiment hai: wahi code chroot setup ke against True dena chahiye. Comment: 'If this ever fails, the test above proves nothing.'

M1 ne pivot_root ko chroot se badla: isolation ke 36 tests mein se exactly 1 red hua -- escape test. Baaki 35 green rahe kyunki normal commands ke liye chroot aur pivot_root same dikhte hain. Yani agar escape test na hota toh yeh security-relevant regression kisi ko pata nahi chalta. Result '1' bhejne ke liye 'E' default hai, taaki crash ko pass/fail se alag pehchana ja sake.
why_needed: Negative tests ('yeh nahi hona chahiye') tabhi meaningful hain jab aap prove karo ki test kar sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Metal detector check karne ke liye pehle jaan bujh kar chaabi le kar guzro. Beep nahi hua toh 'koi metal nahi' wala result bhi bekaar.
how_it_works: chroot sirf process ka root pointer badalta hai; kernel '..' ko tabhi rokta hai jab walk root se guzre. cwd bahar ho toh root kabhi cross hi nahi hota. pivot_root namespace ka root mount badal deta hai aur old root detach hone par upar kuch bachta nahi.
in_this_project: Config.use_pivot_root sirf isi test ke liye hai (docstring: 'exists ONLY so a test can prove that difference').
code_example:
# real, tests/integration/test_isolation.py
def test_pivot_root_cannot_be_escaped(rootfs, tmp_path):
    assert _escape_attempt(rootfs, tmp_path, use_pivot_root=True) is False


def test_chroot_alone_can_be_escaped(rootfs, tmp_path):
    # the control experiment: the same escape against chroot DOES reach the host. If this ever
    # fails, the test above proves nothing.
    assert _escape_attempt(rootfs, tmp_path, use_pivot_root=False) is True
advantages: Test ki apni validity proven hai
Security regression ek specific test se pakda jaata hai
disadvantages: Forked child mein asli mounts, sirf Linux + root par
Ek hi escape technique test hoti hai
common_mistakes: Sirf negative test likhna, control nahi
Crash ko 'escape failed = pass' samajh lena (isliye 'E' default)
follow_up_questions: Child mein exception aaye toh test kya karta hai?
Ek aur escape technique ka test kaise likhoge (jaise mount sysfs)?

question: What happened when mutation M4 removed 'make every mount private first', and why does that one line matter so much on a systemd host?
answer_hinglish:
Plan ka step 1 hai mount(NULL, '/', MS_REC|MS_PRIVATE). Server par read-only check mein dekha gaya tha ki / 'shared' mount hai (systemd default). Shared propagation ka matlab: ek namespace mein jo mount hota hai woh peer group ke doosre namespaces mein bhi propagate hota hai. Naye mount namespace (CLONE_NEWNS) ke mounts bhi peer bane rehte hain jab tak aap unhe private na karo.

M4 mein yeh step hataya (18:18, 'as predicted'). Do cheezein hui: container ke overlay, proc, /dev tmpfs, devpts aur shm mounts host namespace mein propagate ho gaye -- /proc/mounts mein 10 extra lines -- aur pivot_root ne shared mount ko refuse kar diya (EINVAL), toh container setup fail. 2 tests red + 2 errors (no_leftovers fixture ne host mein mounts dekhe). Mounts haath se hatane pade: 'sudo umount -R <state>/merged' dono containers ke liye; uske baad /proc/mounts wapas 29 lines, 0 mentioning h16.

Unit level par test_first_step_makes_everything_private assert karta hai ki plan ka pehla step exactly yahi Mount hai, overlay ke saath bhi aur bina bhi. Integration level par fixture host mounts check karta hai.
why_needed: Mount propagation woh bug hai jo container ke bahar host ko ganda karta hai; yeh samajhna runtime likhne ke liye basic hai.
real_world_analogy: Shared Google Doc: aapne apni copy samjh kar edit kiya, lekin woh 'linked' thi aur sabke paas badal gaya. Pehle 'make a copy' (private) karo.
how_it_works: Har mount ka propagation type hota hai: shared, slave, private, unbindable. MS_REC|MS_PRIVATE poore tree ko private bana deta hai sirf is namespace ke liye; host par koi asar nahi. pivot_root ki ek condition hai ki new root aur uska parent shared na hon.
in_this_project: mounts.build_plan ka pehla step; docstring point 1: 'make every mount in the new namespace private, so nothing we mount leaks to the host'. README table row 1 M4 ko reference karti hai.
advantages: Ek line host ko leak se bachati hai
Unit + integration dono level par checked
disadvantages: Bhoolna aasaan, aur effect sirf systemd hosts par dikhta hai
common_mistakes: Sochna ki CLONE_NEWNS akela mounts ko private kar deta hai
Leaked mounts ko umount -R ke bina hatane ki koshish (nested mounts bache rehte hain)
follow_up_questions: Slave propagation kab useful hai (host ke naye mounts container mein dikhein, ulta nahi)?
pivot_root shared mounts ko kyun refuse karta hai?

question: In the first manual run the user's command was PID 3 instead of PID 2. How was this found and what was the cause?
answer_hinglish:
Pehla container haath se chalaya, 'echo $$' ne 3 print kiya -- jabki design ke hisaab se INIT PID 1 aur CMD PID 2 hona chahiye. Toh PID 2 kisne liya? INIT ke andar kuch aur fork hua tha.

Cause: libc.py pehle ctypes.util.find_library('c') use karta tha. Linux par find_library andar se 'ldconfig' ko subprocess ke roop mein chalata hai. Yeh call pehli baar mount ke time hoti hai -- yani INIT ke andar, naye PID namespace mein. Toh woh subprocess PID 2 ban gaya, aur user command PID 3.

Fix (SERVER_RUN.md incident 1): pehle ctypes.CDLL('libc.so.6') seedha try karo (glibc soname), aur sirf fail hone par find_library. Code comment yahi explain karta hai. Isse regression na ho, test_command_is_pid_2_and_init_is_pid_1 assert karta hai ki 'echo $$' 2 hai aur /proc/1/cmdline mein 'minibox' hai.

Debugging lesson: ek 'chhota' symptom (PID number) design invariant tootne ka signal tha. Library calls ke hidden side effects (subprocess, threads) namespace ke andar dikh jaate hain.
why_needed: Hidden subprocess/fork container ke andar PID, cgroup count (pids.max) aur signals sab ko affect karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Party mein aap 2nd guest expect kar rahe the, lekin caterer ka helper pehle ghus gaya aur 2 number ka badge le gaya.
how_it_works: PID namespace mein PIDs 1 se shuru hote hain. Har fork agla number leta hai. find_library ka subprocess ek fork + exec hai, jo pid allocate karta hai aur phir exit -- lekin number already use ho chuka.
in_this_project: libc.py ka libc() function lazily load karta hai; comment: 'inside the container that extra fork would take PID 2 before the user's command does'.
advantages: Fix chhota aur documented
Invariant ab test se protected
disadvantages: musl based host par libc.so.6 nahi milega, fallback phir find_library chalayega
common_mistakes: PID 3 ko cosmetic maan kar ignore karna
Library ko black box maanna jabki woh subprocess chala sakti hai
follow_up_questions: libc ko INIT fork se pehle host process mein load kar lete toh kya hota?
pids.max=1 hota toh yeh hidden fork kya karta?

question: A teammate wants to use minibox on a shared build server to run CI jobs from untrusted pull requests, 'because it has namespaces and cgroup limits'. What do you tell them, using what minibox actually does and does not do?
answer_hinglish:
Jawab: I would recommend a different approach. minibox is kaam ke liye galat tool hai, aur yeh opinion nahi, README ki pehli warning hai.

Kya kaam karega: cgroup limits asli hain aur measured hain -- pids.peak exactly 32 (fork bomb bhi), memory hog 64.0 MiB par OOM kill (exit 137, CONSTRAINT_MEMCG, host affected nahi), cpu share 0.501 at --cpus 0.5. Namespaces se honest jobs ek doosre ki files, PIDs, hostname, IPC nahi dekhte; overlay se image clean rehti hai.

Kya nahi karega: untrusted PR ka code container mein host root hai (no user namespace), saari capabilities ke saath (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_MKNOD), bina seccomp/AppArmor. README khud escape batata hai: mknod host disk, mount it. Matlab ek malicious PR build server ke secrets, doosre jobs ke artifacts, sab padh sakta hai. Plus operational gaps: networking sirf loopback (CI ko dependencies download karni hain), minibox SIGKILL ho toh leaked containers aur cgroups, koi gc nahi, parent cgroup race par exit 125, aur sirf ek foreground command.

Recommendation: untrusted code ke liye VM ya microVM per job (ya gVisor jaisa sandbox), ya kam se kam rootless podman/docker with user namespaces + default seccomp. minibox ko learning aur trusted local experiments tak rakho -- README: 'Run only code you would run as root on the host anyway'.
why_needed: Prototype ko production mein galat jagah use hone se rokna senior engineer ka kaam hai; 'limits work' aur 'secure' alag claims hain.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ke kamron mein taale hain (namespaces) aur bijli ka meter per kamra (cgroups), lekin har mehmaan ke paas main door ki chaabi hai. Ajnabi ko kamra kiraye par nahi doge.
how_it_works: Threat model: CI untrusted code = attacker controlled. Required: privilege isolation (user ns / VM), syscall surface reduction, network egress control, secret isolation, aur cleanup guarantees. minibox sirf resource isolation + view isolation deta hai.
in_this_project: cli.main root maangta hai; setup_container mein CLONE_NEWUSER nahi; test_user_namespace_is_shared_with_the_host limitation pin karta hai. Limits ke numbers README ke MEASURED section se.
code_example:
# real, minibox/cli.py main (trimmed)
if os.geteuid() != 0:
    print("minibox: run needs root (no user namespace support), use sudo", file=sys.stderr)
    return 125
advantages: Resource limits measured aur reliable
Limitations documented, decision easy
disadvantages: Untrusted code ke liye koi privilege isolation nahi
Networking, gc, exec missing
common_mistakes: 'Namespaces hain toh secure hai' maan lena
cgroup limits ko security feature samajhna
Build server ke secrets ko container ke same host par rakhna
follow_up_questions: Agar sirf trusted internal repos ke CI jobs hon toh kya minibox chalega?
Untrusted CI ke liye VM vs gVisor vs rootless containers ka trade-off?
Secrets ko job tak kaise pahunchaoge bina host par expose kiye?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Resource isolation (cgroups) aur privilege isolation (user ns, caps, seccomp, VM) alag axes hain. minibox pehle mein strong, doosre mein zero.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Malicious PR: mknod + mount host disk, secrets read, doosre jobs tamper. Operational: minibox crash par leaked containers; parallel starts par parent cgroup race (exit 125); fork bomb jaise cases mein limits theek hain.
advanced.alternatives: Firecracker/microVM per job, gVisor (runsc), Kata containers, ya rootless podman + user ns + seccomp default.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Sau jobs per ghante: per-job VM ka boot cost vs container ka ~18 ms; isliye industry pooled microVMs use karti hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Agar minibox ko is direction le jaana ho: user ns + caps drop + seccomp + egress-controlled network + gc + per-job outer scope limit -- har ek ke saath escape tests. Tab tak: trusted-only.

question: M17's first version made all 9 limit tests fail. Why was that result rejected as a 'catch', and what does it teach about reading mutation results?
answer_hinglish:
M17 ka idea tha 'cpu.max not written'. Pehle version mein cgroups.py ke Limits.writes() ke ek 'if' block ki EKLAUTI statement hata di gayi -- 'if self.cpus is not None:' ke neeche ki w.append line. Python mein khaali block SyntaxError hai, toh module import hi nahi hua aur limits ke saare 9 tests fail hue.

Yeh 'caught' nahi hai: tests isliye fail hue kyunki code chala hi nahi, isliye nahi ki unhone missing cpu.max pakda. Agar yeh accept karte toh M17 ka result jhootha hota -- shayad cpu.max ka koi test hi na ho, phir bhi 9/9 red. SERVER_RUN.md incident 6: re-run with 'pass' in its place -> 2 failed, jo expected hai (cpu.max se jude tests).

Lesson: mutation result ko count se nahi, REASON se padho. Red tests ka failure message dekho: kya woh mutated rule ke baare mein hai? Similar sanity check: M4 aur M6 ke 'errors' fixture se aaye the, unhe alag likha gaya. Aur mutation se pehle har baar clean tree ship hota tha, taaki pichla mutation leak na kare.
why_needed: Galat reason se red test false confidence deta hai, bilkul galat reason se green test jaisa.
real_world_analogy: Car ki brake test karne ke liye brake wire kaati, lekin galti se engine bhi band ho gaya. Car ruk gayi -- lekin isse brake ke baare mein kuch pata nahi chala.
how_it_works: Valid mutant woh hai jo compile/import ho aur sirf ek behaviour badle. Invalid (stillborn) mutants ko count se bahar rakhna chahiye. Tools jaise mutmut yeh automatically karte hain; hand mutation mein khud dhyan rakhna padta hai.
in_this_project: Limits.writes() pure function hai; cpu.max ka value format_cpu_max se aata hai, 0.5 -> '50000 100000'.
advantages: Re-run se sahi number mila (2 failed)
Incident documented, chhupaya nahi
disadvantages: Hand mutations mein aisi galti aasaan hai
common_mistakes: Mutation ka red count dekh kar seedha 'caught' likh dena
Failure message na padhna
follow_up_questions: Ek automated check kaise banaoge jo stillborn mutant ko pehchane?
Kya 'pass' wala version sabse accha mutant hai, ya 'w.append' ko galat value se likhna better hota?

question: minibox was tested on a shared server that also runs Docker, Caddy and sshd. How was the work kept safe, and how was cleanup PROVEN rather than assumed?
answer_hinglish:
SERVER_RUN.md ka method: 'look before you touch, everything temporary, clean up, prove it'.

Look (17:47:40): ek before-snapshot (hostname, arch, memory, listening ports, iptables INPUT, docker ps, home folder, /opt/node) locally save kiya, repo mein nahi. Read-only checks: cgroup v2 aur root ke subtree_control mein cpu/memory/pids already (taaki minibox root cgroup na badle), overlay in /proc/filesystems, / shared, 29 lines /proc/mounts, 4 GB swap 0 B used, Docker FORWARD aur nat ka owner.

Temporary: sab kuch ~/h16 mein -- pytest wheels PC par pip download (hash checked), tar se ship, PYTHONPATH se use, kabhi install nahi. Koi apt, koi system pip, koi port, koi iptables rule nahi. question: Stage 4 (veth + bridge + NAT) was deliberately not built. What exactly was the reason, and what would the first step be if it is picked up?
answer_hinglish:
PLAN.md ka 'Stage 4 decision'. portfolio-a2 par read-only check: Docker installed hai aur FORWARD chain ka owner hai -- policy DROP, phir DOCKER-USER, DOCKER-FORWARD, phir REJECT -- aur nat table mein Docker ka MASQUERADE rule hai. minibox ke liye bridge + NAT ka matlab tha naye FORWARD aur POSTROUTING rules un chains mein daalna jo Docker manage karta hai. Unhe temporary (save nahi) aur tagged bana sakte the, lekin woh ek shared server par Docker ke rules ke saath baithte, aur brief ne kaha tha risk lene se behtar networking chhod do. SERVER_RUN bhi kehta hai: koi iptables rule add ya change nahi hua.

Aaj kya hai: setup_container CLONE_NEWNET karta hai, aur bring_up_loopback ioctl (SIOCGIFFLAGS/SIOCSIFFLAGS) se lo ko up karta hai, iproute2 ke bina. test_only_loopback_network_and_it_is_up check karta hai ki /proc/net/dev mein sirf 'lo' hai aur ping 127.0.0.1 kaam karta hai. M10 jaisa koi network mutation nahi, lekin namespace test 'net' ko bhi check karta hai.

Agla step (NOT done): veth pair WITHOUT NAT -- ek end host par, ek container namespace mein, ek private /30 par, bilkul koi iptables nahi. Isse host <-> container traffic aata hai bina Docker ki chains ko chhue. Bridge, NAT aur port publishing uske baad.
why_needed: Senior decision: feature skip karna jab risk shared system par ho, aur clear 'next safe step' define karna.
real_world_analogy: Kiraye ke flat mein building ki main wiring (Docker ki chains) nahi chhedte; apne kamre mein extension board (veth /30) laga lete ho.
how_it_works: veth = virtual ethernet pair, ek taraf packet daalo doosri taraf nikalta hai. Ek end ko 'ip link set netns' se container ke namespace mein bhejte hain. Internet ke liye host par forwarding + NAT (MASQUERADE) chahiye, jo iptables/nftables FORWARD aur POSTROUTING mein rules maangta hai.
in_this_project: container.py bring_up_loopback; PLAN.md 'Network' decision: 'Isolation by default; no host network sharing. Stage 4 would add a veth pair.'
code_example:
# real, minibox/container.py
def bring_up_loopback() -> None:
    """ifconfig lo up, with SIOCGIFFLAGS / SIOCSIFFLAGS on a plain socket (no iproute2 needed)."""
    import fcntl  # Linux only; imported here so the module still imports on Windows for unit tests

    siocgifflags, siocsifflags, iff_up = 0x8913, 0x8914, 0x1
    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM) as s:
        ifreq = struct.pack("16sH22x", b"lo", 0)
        flags = struct.unpack("16sH22x", fcntl.ioctl(s.fileno(), siocgifflags, ifreq))[1]
        fcntl.ioctl(s.fileno(), siocsifflags, struct.pack("16sH22x", b"lo", flags | iff_up))

Default isolated network, koi accidental exposure nahi
disadvantages: Container internet se kuch download nahi kar sakta
Port publishing nahi, toh server apps test nahi ho sakte
common_mistakes: Docker ki chains mein rule daal kar 'temporary hai' bolna
Network namespace ko hi chhod dena (host network share)

advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut containers ke liye bridge + IP allocation (IPAM) + per-container veth + NAT/port mapping chahiye -- yeh Docker ka libnetwork / CNI plugins ka kaam hai.
