question: Exercise: minibox has no gc. If minibox itself is SIGKILLed, the container keeps running and its cgroup and state dir stay. Sketch a 'minibox gc' that cleans up safely, reusing the existing code.
answer_hinglish:
Pehle sach: yeh feature NAHI hai. README NOT-done list: 'If minibox itself is SIGKILLed, nobody cleans up: the container keeps running and its cgroup and state dir stay. There is no minibox gc/ps/stop/exec'. Kyun: cleanup host-side run() ke finally mein hai, aur SIGKILL finally nahi chalne deta.

Sketch (exercise, likha nahi gaya): (1) /sys/fs/cgroup/minibox ke har leaf ko list karo. (2) Decide karo ki owner minibox process zinda hai ya nahi -- aaj koi pid file nahi hai, toh pehla code change: run() cgroup create ke baad state dir mein apna host pid aur start time likhe. gc pid + /proc/<pid>/stat ka start time match kare (pid reuse se bachne ke liye). (3) Owner mara hua hai toh Cgroup(name).kill() -- yeh already cgroup.kill likhta hai aur populated 0 ka wait karta hai -- phir Cgroup.remove(), jo parent ko EBUSY/ENOTEMPTY par chhod deta hai. (4) State dir: overlay INIT ke mount namespace mein tha, INIT mara toh mount bhi gaya, toh shutil.rmtree safe hai -- lekin pehle os.path.ismount(merged) check karo, jaise cleanup() karta hai. (5) Owner zinda ho toh kuch mat chhuo.

Edge: no_leftovers fixture bhi yahi pattern karta hai (kill, wait, rmdir), toh gc us logic ka production version hoga. Race: gc aur ek naya container same name -- name uniqueness os.mkdir se already enforce hoti hai.
why_needed: Long-running hosts par crash ke baad leaked cgroups aur dirs jama hote hain; real runtimes (containerd) ke paas shim + state reconciliation isi ke liye hai.
real_world_analogy: Hotel checkout ke baad housekeeping: room ke 'occupied' board (pid file) ko dekh kar hi saaf karo, warna guest ka saamaan phenk doge.
how_it_works: Ownership check (pid + start time), idempotent cleanup (har step ENOENT tolerate kare), aur ordering (pehle kill, phir rmdir cgroup, phir dirs).
in_this_project: Reusable pieces: Cgroup.kill, Cgroup.remove, cleanup() ka ismount guard. Missing piece: owner metadata.
advantages: Existing primitives already idempotent-ish
Crash recovery possible bina daemon ke
disadvantages: Owner metadata nahi hai aaj, toh pehle format design karna padega
Running container ko galti se maarne ka risk
common_mistakes: Sirf pid check karna (pid reuse)
State dir pehle delete karna jab overlay abhi mounted ho
Claim karna ki gc already hai
follow_up_questions: Default state dir /run/minibox reboot par kyun khud saaf ho jaata hai, aur cgroups?
gc ko 'ps' aur 'stop' ke saath kaise jodoge?
Containerd shim yeh problem kaise solve karta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Daemon-less design simple hai lekin crash recovery ke liye on-disk state chahiye. gc explicit command hai, background reconciler nahi.
advanced.failure_scenarios: minibox SIGKILL: container chalta rehta (uski limits cgroup mein bani rehti hain, toh unlimited nahi), lekin koi use rokega nahi. gc galat owner check se zinda container maar sakta hai.
advanced.alternatives: containerd-shim jaisa per-container supervisor jo parent marne par bhi zinda rahe; ya systemd transient unit per container (systemd khud cleanup karta).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Hazaron containers par gc ko directory scan ke bajaye state index chahiye, aur parallel kill.
advanced.production_improvements: pid + start-time metadata, 'minibox ps' jo wahi padhe, gc ka dry-run mode, aur integration test jo minibox ko SIGKILL karke gc chalaye aur no_leftovers jaisa assert kare.

question: List the failure modes minibox does NOT handle, and say what actually happens in each.
answer_hinglish:
README ki honest list se:

(1) minibox khud SIGKILL ho jaaye: host-side run() ka finally nahi chalta. Container chalta rehta hai (INIT ka parent mara, lekin INIT zinda), uska cgroup /sys/fs/cgroup/minibox/<name> aur state dir bache rehte hain. Koi gc/ps/stop nahi. (SIGTERM/SIGINT forward hote hain, toh normal Ctrl-C ya kill theek se band karta hai.)

(2) Shared parent cgroup race: do containers ek saath start ho rahe hain jab aakhri container parent /sys/fs/cgroup/minibox ko rmdir kar raha hai -- doosre ko ENOENT milta hai aur exit 125. Cgroup.create pehle makedirs(parent) karta hai, phir subtree_control likhta hai; beech mein parent gaya toh fail.

(3) Same name: doosra container 125 se fail hota hai aur pehle wale ka cgroup nahi hatata -- yeh HANDLED hai, owned dict ki wajah se, aur test_two_containers_with_the_same_name_cannot_run_at_once check karta hai.

(4) Setup fail (jaise galat workdir): 125, aur state + cgroup clean (test_failed_setup_also_cleans_up).

(5) Not done: exec into running container, TTY (-t) allocation; terminal wala process-group code likha hai lekin test nahi. IO/cpuset limits, memory.high, OOM score nahi. Image config ka Env/Cmd/User ignore. zstd layers nahi.
why_needed: Interviewer 'kya toot sakta hai' poochta hai; jawab mein handled aur unhandled ko alag karke bolna chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Car ka manual: 'ABS hai, airbags hai, lekin spare tyre nahi' -- jo nahi hai uska saaf zikr.
how_it_works: Cleanup finally block mein hai jo exceptions aur normal exit par chalta hai, SIGKILL par nahi. owned flags ensure karte hain ki cleanup sirf apne banaye resources ko chhuye.
in_this_project: run() ka owned = {'cgroup': False, 'state': False} aur comment 'never clean up another container's cgroup/dirs'.
code_example:
# real, minibox/container.py run (trimmed)
owned = {"cgroup": False, "state": False}     # never clean up another container's cgroup/dirs
...
finally:
    ...
    cleanup(cfg, cgroup if owned["cgroup"] else None, state if owned["state"] else None, started, exit_code)
advantages: Handled cases tested
Unhandled cases documented
disadvantages: SIGKILL ke baad manual cleanup chahiye
Parent cgroup race rare lekin real
common_mistakes: Sochna ki finally block SIGKILL par bhi chalta hai
Failed duplicate run ka doosre container ki cgroup hata dena
follow_up_questions: Parent cgroup race ko kaise fix karoge (retry, ya parent kabhi delete na karo)?
SIGKILL ke baad container ki cgroup limits kya ab bhi laagu hain?

question: Why are exec, TTY allocation, IO limits and rootless mode out of scope, and what would each one cost to add to this design?
answer_hinglish:
PLAN.md 'Not in scope' aur README NOT-done list yeh sab kehte hain; ek-ek ka cost design ke hisaab se:

exec: aaj model hai 'one foreground command per container', container ki life = command ki life. exec ke liye chahiye: running container dhoondhna (state/pid file, jo aaj nahi), setns se uske mnt/pid/uts/ipc/net namespaces join karna, cgroup.procs mein daalna. Aur M18 wali baat: exec wala process INIT ka child nahi hoga, toh tab cgroup.kill asli kaam karega.

TTY (-t): pty pair banana, slave ko container ke /dev/pts (jo newinstance devpts hai) se jodna, host par master se copy loop, window resize (SIGWINCH). Aaj sirf yeh hai: agar stdin terminal hai toh CMD apna process group leta hai aur tcsetpgrp karta hai, taaki Ctrl-C sirf command ko jaaye -- lekin yeh path test nahi hua kyunki tests terminal ke bina chalte hain.

IO limits: cgroup v2 io.max device major:minor maangta hai; Limits.writes() mein ek aur pair. Root ke subtree_control mein io already hai (server check), lekin CONTROLLERS tuple sirf cpu, memory, pids hai.

Rootless: user namespace + uid mapping, cgroup delegation (systemd), overlay ka unprivileged mount, aur networking. Sabse mehenga, kyunki cli.main hi root check karta hai aur poora design root maanta hai.
why_needed: Scope cut karna aur har cut ka cost bata paana senior engineer ki nishani hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar banate waqt pehle foundation aur deewarein; lift aur solar baad mein -- lekin naksha mein jagah chhodo.
how_it_works: Har feature runtime ke ek naye axis ko chhoota hai: exec = namespace join (setns), tty = terminal subsystem, io = cgroup controller, rootless = privilege model.
in_this_project: init_main ka isatty branch; cgroups.CONTROLLERS = ('cpu', 'memory', 'pids'); cli.main ka geteuid check.
code_example:
# real, minibox/container.py init_main (trimmed): the written but untested terminal path
if os.isatty(0):
    # Own process group in the terminal's foreground: Ctrl-C then reaches only the
    # command (as when it runs without minibox), not minibox and INIT as well.
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTTOU, signal.SIG_IGN)
    os.setpgid(0, 0)
    os.tcsetpgrp(0, os.getpgrp())
advantages: Core (namespaces, cgroups, overlay, pull) poori tarah tested
Har missing feature ka cost samjha hua
disadvantages: Interactive use (shell with -t) aur debugging (exec) nahi
Untested terminal code path
common_mistakes: Untested code ko 'supported' bolna
exec ko sirf 'nsenter chala do' samajhna, cgroup aur PID ns join bhool kar
follow_up_questions: setns se PID namespace join karne par current process kyun nahi badalta?
io.max ke liye device number kaise nikaloge overlay root par?
Rootless mein cgroup limits kaise milte hain?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Chhota scope = har feature ke liye test + mutation possible. Badla mein minibox docker run ka sirf non-interactive subset hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Untested isatty path real terminal mein galat behave kar sakta hai (jaise SIGTTOU ya process group issue) aur koi test nahi pakdega. exec bina cgroup join ke limits bypass karega.
advanced.alternatives: exec ke liye nsenter-style setns; tty ke liye runc ka console socket model; rootless ke liye podman ka slirp4netns + fuse-overlayfs + newuidmap.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada users par rootless almost zaroori hai (har user ko root nahi de sakte); exec/ps/stop ke liye state store aur ek manager process chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Pehle state metadata (pid file), phir ps/stop/gc, phir exec; tty ke liye pty-based integration test (pty module se) taaki isatty path cover ho.

question: Why write a container runtime in Python with ctypes and zero dependencies instead of Go like runc? Where does that choice hurt?
answer_hinglish:
PLAN.md ka pehla decision: Python 3.12, zero third-party runtime dependencies (pyproject 'dependencies = []  # stdlib only, on purpose'). Stdlib mein os.unshare, os.fork, os.execvpe, os.chroot, os.mknod, socket.sethostname already hain; sirf mount(2), umount2(2) aur pivot_root(2) ctypes se libc par jaate hain (libc.py, PLAN ke hisaab se about 60 lines). pivot_root ka glibc wrapper hi nahi, toh syscall number se call: x86_64 155, aarch64 41. PLAN khud likhta hai: 'Go or C would be the production choice (runc is Go); Python keeps every syscall visible and the code short.' Image pull bhi urllib + hashlib + tarfile mein ~250 lines.

Fayde: learning project ke liye har syscall ek line mein dikhta hai; zero deps se server par install nahi karna pada (sirf pytest PYTHONPATH se); unit tests Windows par.

Kahan dard: (1) Startup -- 18 ms inner lekin 105 ms outer, yani ~87 ms sirf Python interpreter. (2) fork in Python: interpreter state duplicate hoti hai, aur hidden library side effects -- PID 3 bug isi ka example (find_library ne subprocess chalaya). (3) Go ke liye bhi runc ko C 'nsexec' chahiye kyunki multi-threaded runtime mein unshare unsafe hai; Python single-threaded hai toh yeh problem yahan nahi aayi, ek accidental fayda. (4) seccomp, capset, netlink, clone3 ke liye stdlib mein kuch nahi -- har ek ke liye aur ctypes. (5) Syscall numbers aur struct layouts (ifreq '16sH22x') haath se, architecture ke hisaab se.
why_needed: Language choice ko goal (learning vs production) se jodna system design ka basic hai.
real_world_analogy: Car engine samajhne ke liye transparent glass model banana (Python) vs race ke liye asli engine (Go/C).
how_it_works: ctypes CDLL('libc.so.6', use_errno=True) libc load karta hai; argtypes set karke C function call; errno ctypes.get_errno() se. syscall() generic entry hai jab wrapper na ho.
in_this_project: libc.py: SYS_PIVOT_ROOT dict, mount/umount2 wrappers, _check jo errno ko OSError banata hai. MS_* flags header values se, aur test_mount_flag_values_match_linux_headers unhe check karta hai.
code_example:
# real, minibox/libc.py
def pivot_root(new_root: str, put_old: str) -> None:
    nr = SYS_PIVOT_ROOT.get(platform.machine())
    if nr is None:
        raise OSError(f"pivot_root: unknown syscall number for {platform.machine()}")
    c = libc()
    c.syscall.restype = ctypes.c_long
    _check(c.syscall(ctypes.c_long(nr), _b(new_root), _b(put_old)), f"pivot_root({new_root!r}, {put_old!r})")
advantages: Har syscall readable
Zero install footprint
Unit tests anywhere
disadvantages: Interpreter startup ~87 ms
Hardening syscalls ke liye wrappers nahi
Arch-specific numbers haath se
common_mistakes: Sochna ki Python fork 'free' hai -- hidden subprocess/threads
ctypes argtypes set na karna (64-bit flags truncate)
follow_up_questions: Go runtime mein unshare(CLONE_NEWNS) direct kyun problem hai aur runc kaise bachta hai?
Startup 105 ms se kam karna ho toh kya karoge?
Python mein seccomp filter kaise load karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Visibility + zero deps vs performance + ecosystem. Learning ke liye Python sahi; production mein startup aur missing primitives (seccomp, netlink) dard denge.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Galat syscall number naye arch par -> 'unknown syscall number' OSError (safe fail). musl host par libc.so.6 nahi -> find_library fallback, jo PID 3 jaisa side effect la sakta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Go + small C preamble (runc ka nsexec), Rust (youki), C (crun -- fast startup). Ya existing runc ko OCI bundle dekar chalao.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 100x containers per second par 105 ms outer startup bottleneck; ek long-running daemon (Python bhi) interpreter cost ek baar deta, phir har container ~18 ms.
advanced.production_improvements: Daemon mode ya crun-jaisa compiled runtime; agar Python hi rakhna ho toh libseccomp ctypes binding aur netlink socket code, aur arch table ko tests se cover karna.

question: Compare minibox's architecture with the real docker stack (docker CLI, dockerd, containerd, shim, runc). Which layer does minibox correspond to?
answer_hinglish:
Docker stack layers mein hai: docker CLI -> dockerd (API, images, networks, volumes) -> containerd (image store, snapshots, container lifecycle) -> containerd-shim (har container ka chhota supervisor, jo parent marne par bhi zinda rehta hai aur exit code rakhta hai) -> runc (OCI runtime: config.json padh kar namespaces, cgroups, mounts, pivot_root, caps, seccomp set karke exec, phir khud exit).

minibox in sab ko ek process mein squash karta hai. 'minibox pull' containerd ke image/content store jaisa kaam karta hai (manifest, index -> platform, digest + diff_id verify, layers ko EK directory mein flatten). 'minibox run' runc + shim dono: host process runc jaisa setup karta hai (cgroup leaf, overlay dirs, unshare, fork) aur shim jaisa rehta hai (wait, signal forward, exit code, cleanup). INIT tini / docker run --init jaisa hai (PID 1 duties).

Bade farak: (1) Koi daemon nahi -- isliye ps/stop/exec/gc nahi, aur SIGKILL ke baad koi recover nahi karta. (2) OCI runtime-spec config.json nahi; CLI flags seedhe Config dataclass banate hain. (3) Layers flattened, docker ki tarah har layer ek overlay lowerdir nahi, toh images ke beech disk sharing nahi. (4) Networking, security hardening nahi. (5) Ek hi foreground command; runc ke paas create/start alag phases hain.

Interview line: minibox 'runc + shim + tini ka teaching version' hai, ek pull client ke saath.
why_needed: Container ecosystem ke layers samajhna Kubernetes, CRI aur debugging ke liye zaroori hai.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant: waiter (CLI), manager (dockerd), kitchen supervisor (containerd), har table ka attendant (shim), aur chef jo dish bana kar chala jaata hai (runc). minibox ek dhaba hai jahan ek hi aadmi sab karta hai.
how_it_works: runc ka model: create (namespaces + init process jo exec se pehle ruka hai) -> start (exec user process). minibox mein bhi INIT pipe par rukta hai jab tak cgroup join ho -- runc ke sync pipe jaisa idea.
in_this_project: container.py docstring teen processes dikhata hai; registry.pull aur image.apply_layer image side; mounts.build_plan runc ke config.json mounts list jaisa data hai.
code_example:
# real, minibox/container.py module docstring (trimmed)
#   minibox (host)        creates the cgroup and overlay dirs, unshare(CLONE_NEWPID), forks INIT,
#     |                   moves INIT into the cgroup, forwards signals, waits, cleans up
#     +- INIT  (PID 1)    unshare(mount, UTS, IPC, net), hostname, mounts, pivot_root, forks CMD,
#          |              then reaps every zombie and forwards signals until CMD exits
#          +- CMD (PID 2) execvp(the user's command)
advantages: Poora path ek jagah padh sakte ho
Har layer ka core idea present
disadvantages: Koi daemon/state nahi
OCI spec compatible nahi
No layer sharing
common_mistakes: containerd aur runc ko same cheez samajhna
Sochna ki dockerd container process ka parent hai (asal mein shim hai)
follow_up_questions: Shim kyun zaroori hai jab runc exit kar jaata hai?
Kubernetes CRI is stack mein kahan fit hota hai?
minibox ko OCI runtime banane ke liye kya badalna padega?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Ek-process design simple aur debuggable, lekin lifecycle management (detach, restart, ps) ke liye layers chahiye. Docker ne isi liye responsibilities split ki: daemon restart ho toh containers chalte rahein (shim ki wajah se).
advanced.failure_scenarios: minibox crash = container orphan + leaked cgroup. Docker mein dockerd crash par bhi shim container ko sambhalta hai aur containerd reconnect karta hai.
advanced.alternatives: OCI bundle (rootfs + config.json) generate karke runc/crun ko dena; ya podman jaisa daemonless model jo conmon (shim jaisa) use karta hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Ek host par sau containers ke liye image store sharing (per-layer lowerdirs), snapshotter, aur ek API daemon chahiye; kai hosts ke liye orchestrator (Kubernetes) CRI ke through.
advanced.production_improvements: Teen kaam alag karo: image store (content-addressed, layer dedup), runtime (OCI spec), supervisor (shim-jaisa, state file + exit code). minibox ka build_plan data model OCI mounts list mein naturally map hota hai.

question: If minibox had to run many containers per host in production, what would have to change? Be specific about what exists today.
answer_hinglish:
Aaj ka measured baseline: empty container ~18 ms inner / 105 ms outer; limits kernel se exact (pids.peak 32, OOM 137 at 64.0 MiB, cpu 0.501 at 0.5). Isolation ka core sahi hai. Production ke liye gaps:

(1) Security pehle: user namespaces, caps drop, seccomp, LSM, masked paths, no_new_privs -- aaj kuch nahi, aur yeh multi-tenant ke liye non-negotiable. (2) Lifecycle + state: aaj koi daemon/state nahi. Chahiye: state store (pid, start time, config), ps/stop/exec, aur gc jo crash ke baad leaked cgroups/dirs saaf kare. Supervisor (shim-jaisa) taaki manager restart par containers na marein. (3) Images: aaj har pull complete hota hai, koi cache nahi, layers ek directory mein flatten. Chahiye: content-addressed layer store, per-layer overlay lowerdirs (disk sharing), zstd, image config ka Env/Cmd/User use. (4) Networking: aaj sirf lo. Chahiye: veth + bridge + IPAM + NAT/port mapping, apni firewall table. (5) Resources: io.max, cpuset, memory.high, OOM score; aur parent cgroup race (ENOENT -> 125) fix -- parent ko kabhi delete na karna sabse simple. (6) Startup: 105 ms ka bada hissa interpreter hai; daemon mode se ek baar. (7) Observability: --stats-file aaj exit par counters deta hai; live metrics (cpu.stat, memory.events) export chahiye.

Honest recommendation: production mein minibox ko badhane ke bajaye containerd + runc/crun use karo; minibox ki value yeh samajhna hai ki woh kya karte hain.
why_needed: System design interview mein 'prototype -> production' gap ko structured tareeke se bolna aata hona chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ki kitchen mein khana sahi banta hai; restaurant chalane ke liye licence, inventory, staff schedule, fire safety -- recipe wahi, system alag.
how_it_works: Production runtime = isolation primitives + security policy + lifecycle state machine + image store + network plumbing + resource accounting + observability.
in_this_project: Cgroup.stats() limits ko kernel se read BACK karta hai aur counters deta hai -- observability ki shuruaat. Cgroup.remove parent ko EBUSY/ENOTEMPTY/ENOENT par chhod deta hai, lekin create side ka race documented hai.
advantages: Core isolation aur limits measured aur correct
Clear gap list already README mein
disadvantages: Production ke liye bahut layers missing
Security gap sabse bada
common_mistakes: Performance ko pehli priority banana jabki security missing hai
Flattened layers ko scale par theek maan lena
follow_up_questions: Parent cgroup race ko permanently kaise hatao ge?
Per-layer lowerdirs se overlay mount options par kya limit aati hai?
Live metrics ke liye kaunse cgroup files poll karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Har production feature (daemon, state, network) complexity aur failure modes laata hai jo aaj ke single-process design mein nahi hain. Isliye industry ne kaam containerd/runc/CNI mein baanta.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Scale par: leaked cgroups crash ke baad jama, parent cgroup race zyada baar, har pull poora download (bandwidth), har image poori copy (disk).
advanced.alternatives: containerd + runc/crun + CNI plugins; ya podman (daemonless + conmon). minibox ka role: learning aur debugging intuition.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x: layer cache + gc + parent cgroup kabhi delete na ho. 100x: daemon (startup amortize), snapshotter, IPAM, metrics pipeline, aur security defaults on.
advanced.production_improvements: Order: security layers -> state + gc -> image cache/layer sharing -> networking -> io/cpuset limits -> metrics. Har step ke saath integration test + mutation check, jaise aaj ke 29.

question: Exercise: write a unit test (runnable on Windows) that proves no step of the mount plan ever touches a path outside the new root. Why is this possible without Linux?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki mounts.build_plan pure hai: woh kuch mount nahi karta, sirf steps ki list (Mount, Mkdir, Mknod, Symlink dataclasses) return karta hai. Toh test plain Python data par chal sakta hai, kisi bhi OS par.

Rule: step 1 (mount(NULL, '/', MS_REC|MS_PRIVATE)) ko chhod kar har step ka target new_root ke andar hona chahiye. Agar koi step galti se '/dev' (host ka) ya '/proc' par mount kare toh woh host ke namespace view ko badal sakta hai ya image directory mein node bana sakta hai. Repo mein yeh test hai: test_every_target_is_inside_new_root -- dono plans (bina overlay aur overlay ke saath) ke liye plan.steps[1:] par loop, Mount ka target ya baaki ka path lo, aur assert karo ki woh new_root hai ya new_root + os.sep se shuru hota hai. os.sep use karna Windows par bhi test ko sahi rakhta hai, aur '+ os.sep' se '/srv/img/rootfs2' jaisa prefix trap pakda jaata hai.

Isi family ke aur tests: test_dev_has_exactly_the_minimal_devices check karta hai ki har Mknod /dev ke tmpfs ke BAAD aata hai (warna node image mein ban jaata), aur test_root_before_proc_before_dev_and_oldroot_last order pin karta hai.
why_needed: Path bugs ka asar host par hota hai; inhe Linux server ke bina pakadna sasta aur safe hai.
real_world_analogy: Moving truck load karne se pehle checklist padh lo ki har dabba naye ghar ke address ka hai -- truck chalaye bina.
how_it_works: Functional core: plan = data. Property-style assertion: 'har element ek condition maane'. Prefix check mein separator jodna zaroori hai warna sibling directory bhi match ho jaati.
in_this_project: tests/unit/test_mounts.py ROOT ko os.path.join(os.sep, 'srv', 'img', 'rootfs') se banata hai, taaki Windows par bhi path separators sahi rahein.
advantages: Milliseconds mein, kisi bhi OS par
Dono plan variants cover
disadvantages: Plan ka intent check hota hai, kernel ka behaviour nahi
Symlink TARGETS (jaise /proc/self/fd) is check mein nahi -- woh container ke andar resolve hote hain
common_mistakes: startswith(new_root) bina os.sep ke likhna
Step 1 ko bhi check mein daal dena (woh jaan bujh kar '/' hai)
follow_up_questions: Symlink ke target ko yeh test kyun ignore karta hai, aur kya yeh sahi hai?
Ek test likho jo check kare ki .oldroot Mkdir hamesha aakhri step hai.

question: How do you design tests for limits that are DANGEROUS if the limit is broken (fork bomb, memory hog), especially when you also run mutation testing against them?
answer_hinglish:
minibox ne do category banayi. Bounded tests: test_spawning_past_pids_max_fails sirf 100 background sleeps chalata hai (comment: 'bounded on purpose (100 sleepers), so it is also safe to run when the limit is NOT written'); memory hog string ko 2^27 bytes (128 MiB) tak double karta hai -- limit se bahut upar, lekin bounded, toh limit na ho tab bhi server nahi girta. Yeh tests mutation runs mein safe hain aur M14/M16 jaise mutants pakadte hain.

Unbounded test: test_fork_bomb_is_stopped_by_pids_max asli bomb chalata hai aur strong guarantee deta hai -- pids.peak exactly 32, refused forks >= 1, 30 s ke andar khatam, aur host abhi bhi /bin/true chala sakta hai. Lekin limit toot jaaye toh yeh server ko gira sakta hai. Rule: yeh HAR mutation run se deselect hota hai, aur README likhta hai ki yeh kabhi mutated code ke against jaan bujh kar nahi chala.

Yeh rule M13 wale incident (SERVER_RUN incident 4) ke baad bana. Design principles: (1) destructive test ko sirf tab chalao jab guard proven ho; (2) har danger ke liye ek bounded twin rakho jo mutation ke liye use ho; (3) outer limit (session scope, ya systemd-run scope) blast radius ko cap kare; (4) timeouts (box.run timeout=30). UTS mutation bhi isi wajah se nahi chala: bina naye UTS namespace ke sethostname asli server ka naam badal deta.
why_needed: Kuch tests khud hathiyar hote hain; unka design safety ke saath karna senior skill hai.
real_world_analogy: Crash test ke liye asli car + dummy use karte ho, asli driver nahi; aur test track ke charo taraf barrier.
how_it_works: Bounded workload ka resource use limit ke bina bhi finite hai, toh failure 'test red' hota hai, 'server down' nahi. Unbounded workload ka resource use sirf limit se rukta hai.
in_this_project: bench/limits.py mein bhi SPAWN (100 sleepers) aur BOMB dono hain, aur bench sirf clean commit 13f7698 par chala. Fork bomb ke measured numbers: pids.peak 32, refused 31 (29-64), ~27 ms.
code_example:
# real, tests/integration/test_limits.py (trimmed)
def test_spawning_past_pids_max_fails(box, tmp_path):
    # bounded on purpose (100 sleepers), so it is also safe to run when the limit is NOT written
    sf = tmp_path / "s.json"
    r = box.run("i=0; while [ $i -lt 100 ]; do sleep 5 & i=$((i+1)); done; echo all-started",
                "--pids", "32", "--stats-file", str(sf))
    s = stats(sf)["counters"]
    assert "all-started" not in r.stdout
    assert s["pids.peak"] == 32 and s["pids.events"]["max"] >= 1
advantages: Mutation coverage bina server risk ke
Real fork bomb guarantee bhi clean code par milti hai
disadvantages: Fork bomb test mutation se bahar, toh uski 'test quality' mutation se proven nahi
Deselect rule runner mein hai, repo mein enforce nahi
common_mistakes: Destructive test ko normal suite ki tarah har jagah chalana
Sirf bounded test rakhna aur asli bomb kabhi na chalana (weak guarantee)
Outer limit ke bina experiment karna
follow_up_questions: Fork bomb test ko ek pytest marker se auto-deselect kaise karoge?
systemd-run --scope -p TasksMax se test run ko kaise wrap karoge?
Memory hog ko bounded rakhne ke liye 2^27 hi kyun?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Strong guarantee (asli bomb) vs safety (bounded twin). Dono rakhe: bounded mutation ke liye, unbounded sirf clean code par. Cost: fork bomb ka apna test mutation se validate nahi.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Guard toot jaaye aur destructive test chal jaaye: M13 incident, load average 3172. Outer limit na hota toh server unresponsive.
advanced.alternatives: Destructive tests ek throwaway VM mein; ya pytest marker 'destructive' + runner jo mutation mode mein unhe skip kare; ya har test run systemd-run --scope ke andar TasksMax/MemoryMax ke saath.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: CI fleet mein ek bhi runaway job shared runner ko gira sakta hai; isliye per-job cgroup limits standard practice hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Repo mein 'destructive' marker add karna aur conftest mein env var (jaise mutation mode) par auto-skip; test runner ko outer scope ke andar chalana; aur incident ke rule ko code mein encode karna, sirf docs mein nahi.
